metadata.title: PISA 2022 Results Volume III: Creative Minds, Creative Schools Factsheets – Greece

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This factsheet reports PISA 2022 results for Greece using OECD’s PISA 2022 Database. The underlying PISA design is a complex, multi-stage sampling of schools and students, and OECD typically applies sampling weights to produce population-representative estimates for 15-year-olds in participating countries/economies. The factsheet does not specify the exact weight variable name (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or whether replicate weights (e.g., BRR/jackknife) were used, so the specific implementation details are not recoverable from the provided text. For interpretation, the reported differences and uncertainty statements (e.g., 95% confidence intervals) indicate that OECD’s standard complex-survey estimation procedures were used, but the exact weighting/replication parameters are not documented in this excerpt.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a country factsheet summarizing published PISA 2022 results rather than an empirical analysis paper that models student-level outcomes with explicitly documented PV and missing-data procedures. The dependent quantities reported (e.g., mean scores on the PISA Creative Thinking scale, proficiency shares, and associations with mathematics/reading) are derived from OECD’s PISA scaling and reporting pipeline, but the excerpt does not describe how plausible values were combined or how missing responses were handled. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling are not reported in the provided text, and the omission reflects a reporting gap at the factsheet level rather than a statement that PVs/missingness were not relevant.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The factsheet reports the analytic sample for Greece as 6,403 students in 230 schools who completed the assessment in mathematics, reading or science, representing about 98,100 15-year-olds in Greece. No additional inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., grade restrictions beyond the PISA target age, item completion thresholds, or missing-data exclusions) are specified in the provided excerpt; it presents the Greece sample used for the PISA 2022 creative thinking reporting.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Volume III (Creative Minds, Creative Schools) factsheet summarizes Greece’s performance on the PISA Creative Thinking cognitive test for 15-year-olds. The creative thinking assessment comprises 32 open-ended tasks measuring three ideation processes (generating diverse ideas, generating creative ideas, evaluating and improving ideas) across four domain contexts (written expression, visual expression, social problem solving, scientific problem solving). In Greece, students’ mean creative thinking score is 27 on a 60-point scale, which is significantly below the OECD average (33). Greece shows a relative pattern aligned with mathematics performance (32% of creative thinking variance uniquely explained by mathematics; correlations of 0.69 with mathematics and 0.65 with reading), and socio-economic status is a strong predictor (explaining 12% of variation). The factsheet also reports proficiency shares (64% at Level 3+; 9% at Level 5/6) and highlights gender differences (girls +2.9 points) and associations with creativity-related beliefs and school pedagogies. Because this is a descriptive results factsheet, no ML model training or predictive evaluation is conducted in the excerpt, and causal claims cannot be inferred from the reported associations.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This extraction is for an OECD PISA 2022 results factsheet (a descriptive reporting product), not an empirical ML study. As such, there is no student-level ML pipeline, no explicitly documented PV-combination or missing-data procedure in the excerpt, and no model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/AUC/RMSE) to populate main_findings. The sparse methodological fields are therefore due to the document’s purpose (summary reporting of OECD-scaled results) rather than missing information about an ML analysis.
